title: Wāyid ʿalēk! Saying the opposite
goal: In the university library, Sēf turns up late to your group project with one slide; tease him with irony, then share out the rest of the work
tip: Irony says the opposite with a straight face. To a friend who has done almost nothing: wāyid ʿalēk! 'steady on, don't overdo it!' (lit. it's too much for you). Mock sympathy works the same way: sāʿtēn? yā ḥalīlak! 'two hours? you poor thing!'. Use it with friends who can laugh back.
grammar: irony: saying the opposite of what you mean (wāyid ʿalēk)
dialogue: A
هلا! سوري تأخرت، بس ترا خلصت الشريحة حقي
hala! sōri taʼakhkhart, bas tara khallaṣt ish-sharīḥa ḥaggi
Hi! Sorry I'm late, but I've finished my slide, you know.
B
شريحة وحدة في أسبوع؟ وايد عليك!
sharīḥa waḥda fi usbūʿ? wāyid ʿalēk!
One slide in a week? Steady on, don't wear yourself out! (ironic)
A
لا تتطنز علي! سهرت عليها، خذت مني ساعتين
la titṭannaz ʿalay! sihart ʿalēha, khadhat minni sāʿtēn
Don't make fun of me! I stayed up late on it; it took me two hours.
B
ساعتين؟ يا حليلك! لازم ترتاح الحين
sāʿtēn? yā ḥalīlak! lāzim tirtāḥ il-ḥīn
Two hours? You poor thing! You must have a rest now. (ironic)
A
خلاص، فهمت! وشو تبيني أسوي في الباقي؟
khalāṣ, fhimt! w shu tabīni asawwi fi l-bāgi?
All right, I get it! So what do you want me to do with the rest?
B
الخاتمة عليك، وتقدم العرض قدام الدكتور
il-khātma ʿalēk, w tgaddim il-ʿarẓ jiddām id-daktōr
The conclusion's yours, and you give the presentation in front of the lecturer.
A
بروحي؟ خيبة! يعني انت ما بتقول ولا كلمة؟ تعال حبيبي!
b-rūḥi? khēba! yaʿni inta ma bitgūl wala kilma? taʿāl ḥabībi!
On my own? Come off it! So you won't say a single word? Nice try, mate!
B
أمزح وياك. أنا بقدم النص الأول
amzaḥ wiyyāk. ana bagaddim in-nuṣṣ il-awwal
I'm joking. I'll present the first half.
A
زين. والكرك علي بعدين، عشان ما تقول إني ما سويت شي
zēn. w il-karak ʿalay baʿdēn, ʿashān ma tgūl inni ma sawwēt shay
Fine. And the karak's on me afterwards, so you can't say I did nothing.
B
كرك بعد؟ ما شاء الله، وايد عليك اليوم!
karak baʿad? mā shāʼ allāh, wāyid ʿalēk il-yōm!
Karak too? Wow, you're really overdoing it today! (ironic)
items: (ironic) steady on, don't overdo it! (to a man) (friends only)
to a woman: wāyid ʿalēch (وايد عليج); lit. 'it's too much for you', said when someone has done very little
don't make fun of me (to a man)
to a woman: la titṭannazīn ʿalay (لا تتطنزين علي)
I stayed up late on it (f.), I worked on it into the night
(recognise); a masculine thing: khadh minni (خذ مني)
the conclusion (of a talk or an essay)
the second half: in-nuṣṣ ith-thāni (النص الثاني)
(sarcastic) nice try, mate! come off it! (to a man) (friends only)
(recognise); to a woman: taʿāli ḥabībti (تعالي حبيبتي); said straight, it's a friendly 'come here, mate'
so (that) you can't say, so you won't say (to a man)
to a woman: ʿashān ma tgūlīn (عشان ما تقولين)
culture: Wāyid ʿalēk works because everyone knows it means the opposite of its words: said with a straight face to a friend who has done very little, it's a joke, not praise. Khēba is the same kind of word, for good-natured teasing among friends. Irony like this belongs with friends your own age; with elders, a manager or someone you've just met, say things straight.

title: Nice parking, champ! Mock praise
goal: Outside Bū Rāshid's majlis, Rāshid praises your terrible parking; take the joke, and tease him back about his team's defeat
tip: Mock praise uses real compliments for something bad: yā baṭal 'champ', yā najim 'superstar', innak fannān 'you're an artist'. The tone and the situation tell everyone it's a joke. When you've both scored a point, call it even: tʿādalna, wāḥid wāḥid.
grammar: irony: mock praise (yā baṭal, yā najim, innak fannān)
dialogue: A
يا سلام! صفيت السيارة عدل، ما شاء الله عليك يا بطل
yā salām! ṣaffēt is-sayyāra ʿadil, mā shāʼ allāh ʿalēk yā baṭal
Wow! You've parked the car so straight; well done, champ! (ironic)
B
أدري، أدري. نص السيارة في الشارع
adri, adri. nuṣṣ is-sayyāra fi sh-shāriʿ
I know, I know. Half the car's in the street.
A
لا، والله إنك فنان! تستاهل جايزة على هالشي
la, wallāh innak fannān! tistāhil jāyza ʿala hash-shay
No, honestly, you're an artist! You deserve a prize for that. (ironic)
B
مشكور يا كابتن. وفريقك؟ سمعت إنكم خسرتوا أمس
mashkūr yā kābtin. w farīgak? simaʿt innakum khisartu ams
Thanks, captain. And your team? I heard you lost yesterday.
A
خيبة! منو قال لك؟ أكيد سيف
khēba! minu gāl-lak? akīd Sēf
Come on! Who told you? It must have been Sēf.
B
محد قال لي. الفيديو في القروب، يا نجم
maḥḥad gāl-li. il-fīdyo fi l-grūb, yā najim
Nobody told me. The video's in the group, superstar. (ironic)
A
زين زين، تعادلنا. واحد واحد
zēn zēn, tʿādalna. wāḥid wāḥid
OK, OK, we're even. One-all.
B
هيه، واحد واحد. بس بعدل السيارة قبل لا يشوفها أبوك
hē, wāḥid wāḥid. bas baʿaddil is-sayyāra gabil la yshūfha ubūk
Yes, one-all. But I'll park the car properly before your dad sees it.
A
تأخرت! شافها من الدريشة، وقام يضحك
taʼakhkhart! shāfha min id-dirīsha, w gām yiẓḥak
Too late! He saw it from the window and burst out laughing.
B
فشلة! بروح أسلم عليه قبل لا يقول شي
fashla! barūḥ asallim ʿalēh gabil la ygūl shay
How embarrassing! I'll go and say hello to him before he says anything.
items: champ! (ironic, for something done badly) (friends only)
you parked the car (to a man); I parked the car
to a woman: ṣaffēti is-sayyāra (صفيتي السيارة)
in the street, on the road
an artist; (ironic) a real artist, a genius
I'll park the car properly, I'll straighten the car

title: The uncle's jokes
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, he jokes that Sēf will come home talking like a foreigner; laugh along, add a joke, stay respectful
tip: When an elder jokes, join in at your own expense or play along with his joke, and never turn it back on him. ana baʿallmah il-ʿarabi 'I'll teach him Arabic' makes him laugh because it's the wrong way round. When he turns serious, follow him: ṣidagt yā ʿammi.
grammar: irony with elders: playing along respectfully (ana baʿallmah il-ʿarabi, ṣār ygūl)
dialogue: A
يا هلا! تعال يا ولدي، نحن قاعدين نضحك على سيف
yā hala! taʿāl yā wildi, niḥin gāʿdīn niẓḥak ʿala Sēf
Welcome! Come in, son; we're having a laugh at Sēf's expense.
B
هلا والله يا عمي. خير؟ شو سوى؟
hala wallāh yā ʿammi. khēr? shu sawwa?
Hello, uncle. What is it? What's he done?
A
سنة في الغربة، وبيرجع يرطن مثل الأجانب، ولا بيعرف يصب القهوة!
sana fi l-ghurba, w biyirjaʿ yirṭin mithil il-ajānib, wala biyaʿrif yṣibb il-gahwa!
A year abroad, and he'll come back jabbering like a foreigner, and won't even know how to pour the coffee!
B
لا تخاف يا عمي، أنا بعلمه العربي!
la tkhāf yā ʿammi, ana baʿallmah il-ʿarabi!
Don't worry, uncle, I'll teach him Arabic!
A
ما شاء الله! الإنقليزي بيعلم ولد دبي العربي؟ هذي يديدة!
mā shāʼ allāh! il-ingilīzi biyʿallim wild Dbayy il-ʿarabi? hādhi yidīda!
Well I never! The Englishman's going to teach a Dubai lad Arabic? That's a new one!
B
والله يا عمي، صار يقول لي سوري بدال آسف
wallāh yā ʿammi, ṣār ygūl-li sōri badāl āsif
Honestly, uncle, he's started saying 'sorry' to me instead of āsif.
A
شفت يا سيف؟ حتى ربيعك صار شاهد عليك!
shift yā Sēf? ḥatta rbīʿak ṣār shāhid ʿalēk!
See, Sēf? Even your friend has become a witness against you!
B
أمزح وياه يا عمي. سيف ما ينسى أهله
amzaḥ wiyyāh yā ʿammi. Sēf ma yinsa ahlah
I'm only teasing him, uncle. Sēf won't forget his family.
A
أدري يا ولدي. المزح حلو، بس الغربة ما فيها مزح
adri yā wildi. il-mazaḥ ḥilu, bas il-ghurba ma fīha mazaḥ
I know, son. Joking's all very well, but being far from home is no joke.
B
صدقت يا عمي. بنشتاق له وايد
ṣidagt yā ʿammi. binishtāg-lah wāyid
That's true, uncle. We'll miss him a lot.
items: (he) jabbers in a foreign language, talks like a foreigner (teasing)
he's started saying, now he says
she's started saying: ṣārat tgūl (صارت تقول)
a witness against you (to a man)
(recognise); to a woman: shāhid ʿalēch (شاهد عليج)
he won't forget his family, he never forgets his family
it's no joke, it's not something to joke about
(recognise); a masculine thing: ma fīh mazaḥ (ما فيه مزح)
a Dubai lad, a son of Dubai
a Dubai girl: bint Dbayy (بنت دبي)
culture: With an elder, banter runs one way. Bū Rāshid may tease Sēf, or you, in front of the majlis; you laugh, play along or joke at your own expense, and you don't tease him back. Friends' words such as yā rayyāl are out of place here: with elders and in official settings they're a real faux pas.

title: Enough now: where banter stops
goal: At a karak stand, Fahad's teasing of Sēf goes too far in front of strangers; step in kindly, stop it, and help Fahad put it right
tip: To stop a joke without a fight: khalāṣ ʿād 'that's enough now', then say why: mub jiddām in-nās 'not in front of people', il-ḥīn mub wagtah 'now's not the time'. zawwadt-ha means 'you went too far', and Fahad uses the same words for 'I went too far' with ḥaggak ʿalay 'I'm sorry'.
grammar: where banter stops: khalāṣ ʿād, zawwadt-ha, mub wagtah
dialogue: A
سيف بيسوق في الغربة؟ هذا اللي رسب في الليسن ثلاث مرات!
Sēf biysūg fi l-ghurba? hādha illi risab fi l-lēsin thalāth marrāt!
Sēf's going to drive abroad? This is the guy who failed his driving test three times!
B
خيبة يا فهد! هذاك من زمان
khēba yā Fahad! hādhāk min zamān
Come off it, Fahad! That was ages ago.
A
وفي المرة الثالثة، المدرب نزل من السيارة وهو يصيح!
w fi l-marra th-thālitha, il-mudarrib nizal min is-sayyāra w huwa yṣīḥ!
(loudly, to the karak man) And the third time, the instructor got out of the car in tears!
B
فهد، خلاص عاد. سيف ما ضحك
Fahad, khalāṣ ʿād. Sēf ma ẓiḥak
Fahad, that's enough now. Sēf isn't laughing.
A
شفيه؟ أمزح! دمه خفيف، يتحمل
shfīh? amzaḥ! dammah khafīf, yitḥammal
What's up with him? I'm joking! He's a good sport, he can take it.
B
يتحمل بيننا، بس مب قدام الناس. زودتها
yitḥammal bēnna, bas mub jiddām in-nās. zawwadt-ha
He can take it between us, but not in front of people. You've gone too far.
A
والله؟ ما كان قصدي أفشله
wallāh? ma kān gaṣdi afashshlah
Really? I didn't mean to embarrass him.
B
أدري. بس الحين مب وقته للمزح. كلمه
adri. bas il-ḥīn mub wagtah lil-mazaḥ. kallmah
I know. But now's not the time for jokes. Talk to him.
A
سيف، حقك علي يا خوي. زودتها
Sēf, ḥaggak ʿalay yā khūy. zawwadt-ha
Sēf, I'm sorry, bro. I went too far.
B
يلا، الكرك اليوم على فهد!
yalla, il-karak il-yōm ʿala Fahad!
(to Sēf) Come on, karak's on Fahad today!
items: you've gone too far (to a man); I went too far
in front of people, in public
(he) can take it, puts up with it
I'm sorry, I owe you an apology (to a man)
to a woman: ḥaggich ʿalay (حقج علي); lit. 'your right is on me'
the driving test; the driving licence (English loan)
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner, talk for 10 minutes about teasing among friends where they grew up: what's fine, and what crosses the line. Tell one short story of a joke that went too far (yours or made up), and use khalāṣ ʿād, zawwadt-ha and ḥaggak ʿalay. Then ask them which jokes they'd never make in front of an elder.

title: The printer hates me: humour at work
goal: At the office, the printer jams again just before a meeting; joke about it with Maryam, keep it polite, and get the copies printed
tip: At work, keep humour light and aim it at things or at yourself: bēni w bēn-ha mushkila gadīma 'it and I have history', ḥaẓẓi 'that's my luck'. Maryam's irony is just as gentle: ḥatta ṭ-ṭābʿa ṣārat titʿallam ʿarabi minnak 'even the printer's learning Arabic from you'.
grammar: light irony at work: joking about yourself (ḥaẓẓi, kill ma)
dialogue: A
الطابعة علقت مرة ثانية؟ شكلها تكرهك
iṭ-ṭābʿa ʿilgat marra thānya? shaklha tikrahak
The printer's jammed again? Looks like it hates you.
B
هيه، بيني وبينها مشكلة قديمة
hē, bēni w bēnha mushkila gadīma
Yes, it and I have history (lit. an old problem between me and it).
A
كل ما تقرب منها تخرب! والله ما شفت جي
kill ma tgarrib minha tikhrab! wallāh ma shift chī
Every time you go near it, it breaks down! Honestly, I've never seen anything like it.
B
حظي. يمكن طفشانة وتبي إجازة مثلي
ḥaẓẓi. yimkin ṭafshāna w tabi ijāza mithli
That's my luck. Maybe it's fed up and wants a holiday, like me.
A
إجازة؟ انت توك راجع من إجازة!
ijāza? inta tawwak rājiʿ min ijāza!
A holiday? You've only just come back from one!
B
صح، بس الطابعة ما تدري. تقدرين تطبعين من فوق؟
ṣaḥḥ, bas iṭ-ṭābʿa ma tadri. tigdarīn tiṭbaʿīn min fōg?
True, but the printer doesn't know that. Could you print upstairs?
A
زين، بطبع النسخ من طابعة الدور الثاني. وانت شوف الورقة اللي علقت
zēn, baṭbaʿ in-nusakh min ṭābʿat id-dōr ith-thāni. w inta shūf il-wurga illi ʿilgat
OK, I'll print the copies on the printer on the second floor. And you look for the paper that's stuck.
B
لقيتها! يمكن كانت تبي أحد يكلمها بالعربي
ligēt-ha! yimkin kānat tabi aḥad ykallimha bil-ʿarabi
Found it! Maybe it wanted someone to talk to it in Arabic.
A
ما شاء الله، حتى الطابعة صارت تتعلم عربي منك!
mā shāʼ allāh, ḥatta ṭ-ṭābʿa ṣārat titʿallam ʿarabi minnak!
Well, well, even the printer's learning Arabic from you now!
B
على الأقل أحد يتعلم مني! مشكورة على النسخ
ʿala l-aqall aḥad yitʿallam minni! mashkūra ʿala n-nusakh
At least someone's learning from me! Thanks for the copies.
items: your luck: ḥaẓẓak (حظك) to a man
a woman, or a feminine thing: ṭafshāna (طفشانة)
the sheet of paper, the paper
culture: Maryam and B joke about the printer, not about each other: humour between colleagues stays light, and it stays polite. Khēba and yā rayyāl are words for friends; a woman colleague, a manager or a client hears plain, friendly Arabic, with mashkūra and mā gaṣṣarti for thanks.

title: I won't do it again
goal: On the phone, Rāshid is cool with you after your joke about his school marks in front of his dad's guests; apologise properly and make it up to him
tip: A real apology after a joke has no excuses: aʿtadhir minnak, ḥaggak ʿalay, ma baʿīd-ha 'I won't do it again'. Say what was wrong (jiddām in-nās), and let him set the terms: lāzim tirẓīni 'you have to make it up to me'. When he says insa s-sālfa, it's over.
grammar: after a joke goes wrong: apologising without excuses (aʿtadhir minnak, ma baʿīd-ha)
dialogue: B
هلا راشد، شحالك؟
hala Rāshid, shḥālak?
Hi Rāshid, how are you?
A
بخير، الله يسلمك. خير؟
b-khēr, allāh ysallmak. khēr?
Fine, thanks. What's up?
B
أبي أعتذر منك. اللي قلته عن درجاتك في المجلس ما كان حلو
abi aʿtadhir minnak. illi giltah ʿan darajātak fi l-majlis ma kān ḥilu
I want to apologise to you. What I said about your marks in the majlis wasn't nice.
A
هيه برو، قدام أبوي والضيوف. حسيت إني ياهل
hē brō, jiddām ubūy w iẓ-ẓyūf. ḥassēt inni yāhil
Yeah, bro, in front of my dad and the guests. I felt like a little kid.
B
معك حق. حقك علي، ما بعيدها
maʿak ḥagg. ḥaggak ʿalay, ma baʿīd-ha
You're right. I'm sorry; I won't do it again.
A
أدري إنك تمزح، بس أبوي ما يمزح في الدرجات
adri innak timzaḥ, bas ubūy ma yimzaḥ fi d-darajāt
I know you were joking, but my dad doesn't joke about marks.
B
فهمت. كان المفروض أمزح وياك بروحنا، مب قدام الناس
fhimt. kān il-mafrūẓ amzaḥ wiyyāk b-rūḥna, mub jiddām in-nās
I get it. I should have joked with you when it was just us, not in front of people.
A
خلاص، انسى السالفة، صفحة يديدة. بس لازم ترضيني: البرجر عليك
khalāṣ, insa s-sālfa, ṣafḥa yidīda. bas lāzim tirẓīni: il-bargar ʿalēk
OK, forget it; clean slate. But you have to make it up to me: the burger's on you.
B
اتفقنا! وولا كلمة عن الدرجات بعد اليوم
ittafagna! w wala kilma ʿan id-darajāt baʿd il-yōm
Deal! And not a word about marks from today on.
A
زين. بس إذا قلت إنك تعرف تلعب كورة، بقول لك: أونه!
zēn. bas idha gilt innak taʿarf tilʿab kūra, bagūl-lak: awinna!
Fine. But if you say you can play football, I'll say: yeah, right!
items: to a woman: aʿtadhir minnich (أعتذر منج)
it wasn't nice, it wasn't right
a feminine thing: ma kānat ḥilwa (ما كانت حلوة)
forget it, let it go (to a man)
to a woman: insay is-sālfa (انسي السالفة)
a clean slate, a fresh start (lit. a new page)
you make it up to me (to a man)

title: Can you do it cheaper?
goal: At the office, a client says your team's offer is too expensive; hold the price politely, and give him something in return for a small discount
tip: Don't drop the price at once. Show what he gets (nkhalliṣ gabl il-mawʿid b-usbūʿ), ask for something back (ʿala sharṭ twaggʿūn il-ʿagid hal-usbūʿ) and keep the respect (ṭāl ʿumrak). ṣaddigni 'believe me' backs a point, but use it once, not in every line.
grammar: negotiating: giving something in return (ʿala sharṭ…, nafs is-siʿir bas…)
dialogue: A
العرض زين، بس السعر غالي شوي. ما تقدرون تنزلون السعر؟
il-ʿarẓ zēn, bas is-siʿir ghāli shwayy. ma tigdarūn tnazzlūn is-siʿir?
The offer's good, but the price is a bit high. Can't you bring it down?
B
نفهمك، طال عمرك. بس صدقني، شغلنا يستاهل
nifhamak, ṭāl ʿumrak. bas ṣaddigni, shughulna yistāhil
We understand, sir. But believe me, our work is worth it.
A
كل الشركات تقول جي. وفي شركة ثانية أرخص منكم
kill ish-sharikāt tgūl chī. w fī sharika thānya arkhaṣ minkum
Every company says that. And there's another company that's cheaper than you.
B
يمكن أرخص، بس بيخلصون على الوقت؟
yimkin arkhaṣ, bas biykhallṣūn ʿala l-wagt?
Maybe cheaper, but will they finish on time?
A
هذا اللي ما أدريه. والميزانية عندنا محدودة، شو بتعطوني زيادة؟
hādha illi ma adrīh. w il-mīzāniyya ʿindana maḥdūda, shu bitaʿṭūni ziyāda?
That I don't know. And our budget's limited; what will you give me on top?
B
نفس السعر، بس نخلص قبل الموعد بأسبوع، والتدريب علينا
nafs is-siʿir, bas nkhalliṣ gabil il-mawʿid b-usbūʿ, w it-tadrīb ʿalēna
The same price, but we finish a week before the deadline, and the training's on us.
A
عرض مب شين. بس أبي خصم بسيط، عشان أقنع المدير عندي
ʿarẓ mub shēn. bas abi khaṣim basīṭ, ʿashān agniʿ il-mudīr ʿindi
Not a bad offer. But I want a small discount, so I can convince my manager.
B
نقدر، على شرط توقعون العقد هالأسبوع
nigdar, ʿala sharṭ twaggʿūn il-ʿagid hal-usbūʿ
We can, on condition you sign the contract this week.
A
اتفقنا. بس لازم أشاور المدير أول
ittafagna. bas lāzim ashāwir il-mudīr awwal
Agreed. But I have to check with my manager first.
B
على راحتك. بنطرش لك العرض الأخير اليوم
ʿala rāḥtak. binṭarrish-lak il-ʿarẓ il-akhīr il-yōm
Take your time. We'll send you the final offer today.
items: you bring the price down (to a group)
to one man: tnazzil is-siʿir (تنزل السعر)
a week before the deadline, a week early
you sign the contract (to a group)
to one man: twaggiʿ il-ʿagid (توقع العقد)

title: Just try it for a month
goal: At the office, persuade your manager, Bū Saʿīd, to try your idea of one shared task list for a month, and answer his doubts
tip: Make a new idea feel safe: keep it small (shahar wāḥid bas, tajruba), say what happens if it fails (lō ma nifaʿ, nirjaʿ lil-īmēl), and offer to do the work yourself (ana basawwīha). Then wait for agnaʿtni 'you've convinced me'.
grammar: persuading: lowering the risk (lō ma nifaʿ…, hal-marra ghēr)
dialogue: B
طال عمرك، عندي فكرة للفريق. تسمح لي دقيقتين؟
ṭāl ʿumrak, ʿindi fikra lil-farīg. tismaḥ-li digīgtēn?
Sir, I've got an idea for the team. Can you spare me two minutes?
A
تفضل، بس بسرعة، عندي اجتماع
tfaẓẓal, bas b-surʿa, ʿindi ijtimāʿ
Go ahead, but quickly; I've got a meeting.
B
بدال الإيميلات اللي صارت فوضى، نحط الشغل كله في قايمة وحدة على النت
badāl il-īmēlāt illi ṣārat fawẓa, nḥuṭṭ ish-shughul killah fi gāyma waḥda ʿala n-nit
Instead of the emails, which have become a mess, we put all the work on one list online.
A
جربنا جي قبل، وما نفع. الكل رجع للإيميل
jarrabna chī gabil, w ma nifaʿ. il-kill rijaʿ lil-īmēl
We tried that before, and it didn't work. Everyone went back to email.
B
هالمرة غير. أنا بسويها، وبعلم الكل عليها
hal-marra ghēr. ana basawwīha, w baʿallim il-kill ʿalēha
This time's different. I'll set it up, and I'll show everyone how to use it.
A
وإذا ضاع وقت الفريق وما استفدنا شي؟
w idha ẓāʿ wagt il-farīg w ma istafadna shay?
And if the team's time is wasted and we've gained nothing?
B
شهر واحد بس، تجربة. لو ما نفع، نرجع للإيميل
shahar wāḥid bas, tajruba. lō ma nifaʿ, nirjaʿ lil-īmēl
Just one month, as a trial. If it doesn't work, we go back to email.
A
كلامك منطقي. بس منو بيتابع الشغل كل أسبوع؟
kalāmak manṭiqi. bas minu biytābiʿ ish-shughul kill usbūʿ?
That makes sense. But who's going to keep track of the work every week?
B
أنا. وكل خميس أطرش لك ملخص
ana. w kill khamīs aṭarrish-lak mulakhkhaṣ
Me. And every Thursday I'll send you a summary.
A
زين، أقنعتني. شهر واحد، وبعدين نشوف
zēn, agnaʿtni. shahar wāḥid, w baʿdēn nshūf
All right, you've convinced me. One month, and then we'll see.
items: can you spare me two minutes? (to a man)
to a woman: tismaḥīn-li digīgtēn? (تسمحين لي دقيقتين؟)
it didn't work, it was no use
a feminine thing: ma nifʿat (ما نفعت)
that makes sense, what you say is logical (to a man)
(recognise); to a woman: kalāmich manṭiqi (كلامج منطقي)
(he) will keep track of, will follow up

title: I'll vouch for him
goal: On the phone, tell your landlord your flatmate is moving out, and persuade him to accept the colleague who'll move in instead
tip: Persuade from your own record: inta taʿarfni min yōm ma sikant 'you've known me since the day I moved in', ʿumri ma taʼakhkhart 'I've never once been late'. Then take the risk on yourself: ana aẓmanah, w ʿala masʼūliyyti 'I'll vouch for him, on my responsibility'.
grammar: persuading from your record (min yōm ma…, ʿumri ma…, ʿala masʼūliyyti)
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم، طال عمرك. أنا سالم، ساكن في شقتك في مردف
as-salāmu ʿalaykum, ṭāl ʿumrak. ana Sālim, sākin fi shiggtak fi Mirdif
Hello, sir. It's Sālim; I live in your flat in Mirdif.
A
وعليكم السلام، هلا يا سالم. آمر؟
wa ʿalaykum is-salām, hala yā Sālim. āmir?
Hello, Sālim. What can I do for you?
B
ربيعي اللي ساكن معاي بيطلع من الشقة آخر الشهر
rbīʿi illi sākin maʿāy biyiṭlaʿ min ish-shigga ākhir ish-shahar
My friend who lives with me is moving out at the end of the month.
A
يعني بتطلع انت بعد؟ ترا أنا أفضل أعطيها عايلة
yaʿni bitiṭlaʿ inta baʿad? tara ana afaẓẓil aʿṭīha ʿāyla
So you're moving out too? I'd rather let it to a family, you know.
B
لا، أنا باقي. وبيسكن معاي زميل من الدوام
la, ana bāgi. w biyiskin maʿāy zamīl min id-dawām
No, I'm staying. And a colleague from work is going to live with me.
A
بس أنا ما أعرفه. ومنو بيضمن لي إنه زين؟
bas ana ma aʿarfah. w minu biyiẓman-li innah zēn?
But I don't know him. And who's going to guarantee me he's all right?
B
أنا أضمنه، وعلى مسؤوليتي. انت تعرفني من يوم ما سكنت
ana aẓmanah, w ʿala masʼūliyyti. inta taʿarfni min yōm ma sikant
I'll vouch for him, on my responsibility. You've known me since the day I moved in.
A
صح، وعمرك ما تأخرت علي في الإيجار
ṣaḥḥ, w ʿumrak ma taʼakhkhart ʿalay fi l-ījār
True, and you've never once been late with the rent.
B
تعال السبت، تشوف الشقة وتتعرف عليه
taʿāl is-sabt, tshūf ish-shigga w titʿarraf ʿalēh
Come on Saturday; you can see the flat and meet him.
A
زين، السبت بعد العصر. وإذا عجبني، نتفاهم
zēn, is-sabt baʿd il-ʿaṣir. w idha ʿajabni, nitfāham
All right, Saturday after ʿaṣr. And if I like him, we'll come to an arrangement.
items: what can I do for you? (lit. command me) (respectful)
I'll vouch for him, I guarantee him
on my responsibility, I'll answer for it
to a woman: inti taʿarfīni (انتي تعرفيني)
task: This week: in Talk, ask your partner to play your landlord, who doesn't want a stranger in his flat. Persuade him for 10 turns, respectfully (ṭāl ʿumrak, ʿala masʼūliyyti, min yōm ma…). Then switch register: record a 2-minute voice note telling Sēf how it went, as friends talk, with a joke or two. Keep to what each person says: no rules, prices or official steps.

title: One condition
goal: At your flat on Saturday, the landlord likes what he sees; agree to his condition, and get your own small request in
tip: When the other side sets a condition, accept it clearly (ma ykhālif, ana l-masʼūl), then make your own request straight away, while he's pleased: bas ʿindi ṭalab ṣaghīr. Keep it small and concrete, and he can agree without losing face.
grammar: negotiating: accepting a condition and asking in return (ma ykhālif…, bas ʿindi ṭalab ṣaghīr)
dialogue: A
ما شاء الله، الشقة نظيفة! أحسن من يوم سلمتك إياها
mā shāʼ allāh, ish-shigga naẓīfa! aḥsan min yōm sallamtak iyyāha
Mā shāʼ allāh, the flat's spotless! Better than the day I handed it over to you.
B
تسلم طال عمرك. أهم شي عندي إنها تبقى جي
tislam ṭāl ʿumrak. ahamm shay ʿindi innha tibga chī
Thank you, sir. What matters most to me is that it stays this way.
A
الله يسلمك. وزميلك، شو شغله؟
allāh ysallmak. w zamīlak, shu shughlah?
You're welcome. And your colleague, what does he do?
B
مهندس في الشركة اللي أتدرب فيها. ريّال محترم وهادي
muhandis fi sh-sharika illi atdarrab fīha. rayyāl miḥtaram w hādi
He's an engineer at the company where I'm an intern. A decent, quiet man.
A
زين. بس عندي شرط: العقد يبقى باسمك، وانت المسؤول
zēn. bas ʿindi sharṭ: il-ʿagid yibga b-ismak, w inta l-masʼūl
Fine. But I have one condition: the contract stays in your name, and you're the one responsible.
B
ما يخالف، أنا المسؤول. بس عندي طلب صغير
ma ykhālif, ana l-masʼūl. bas ʿindi ṭalab ṣghīr
No problem, I'm responsible. But I've got a small request.
A
خير؟ قول
khēr? gūl
What is it? Go on.
B
المكيف في الغرفة الثانية خربان، قبل لا يسكن
il-mkayyif fi l-ghurfa th-thānya kharbān, gabil la yiskin
The AC in the second room is broken; (can it be fixed) before he moves in?
A
هذا حقك. بطرش لك الفني يوم الأحد، واتفقنا
hādha ḥaggak. baṭarrish-lak il-fanni yōm il-aḥad, w ittafagna
That's your right. I'll send you the technician on Sunday, and it's a deal.
B
اتفقنا. وإن شاء الله يسكن السبت الياي
ittafagna. w in shāʼ allāh yiskin is-sabt il-yāy
Deal. And, God willing, he moves in next Saturday.
items: I handed it (f.) over to you (to a man)
(recognise); to a woman: sallamtich iyyāha (سلمتج إياها)
what does he do (for a living)?
what does she do?: shu shughul-ha? (شو شغلها؟)
the one responsible, the person in charge
that's your right, you're entitled to it (to a man)
(recognise); to a woman: hādha ḥaggich (هذا حقج)

title: Time for a new car?
goal: At a karak stand, Sēf says it's time to change your old car and pushes a big one; argue for a small, cheap one, and agree to see a car he knows of
tip: Persuasion between friends goes both ways. Sēf pushes (ismaʿni…, yā shēkh, ish-shakil muhimm); you answer with your own priorities: ish-shakil mub kill shay 'looks aren't everything', ma abi aṣrif wāyid. Before you say yes, check: la ykūn fīha shay? 'there's nothing wrong with it, is there?'
grammar: persuading a friend: pushing and pushing back (ismaʿni…, mub kill shay)
dialogue: A
سيارتك خربت مرة ثانية؟ خلاص يا ريّال، لازم تبدلها
sayyārtak khirbat marra thānya? khalāṣ yā rayyāl, lāzim tbaddilha
Your car's broken down again? That's it, man; you have to change it.
B
أدري، بس ما أبي أصرف وايد
adri, bas ma abi aṣrif wāyid
I know, but I don't want to spend a lot.
A
اسمعني، خذ لك سيارة كبيرة. تروح البر، تروح حتا، ولا شي يوقفك
ismaʿni, khudh-lak sayyāra kbīra. trūḥ il-barr, trūḥ Ḥatta, wala shay ywaggfak
Listen to me, get yourself a big car. You can go to the desert, to Hatta, and nothing will stop you.
B
والبترول؟ أنا أبي وحدة صغيرة
w il-batrōl? ana abi waḥda ṣghīra
And the petrol? I want a small one.
A
صغيرة؟ يا شيخ! الكبيرة تاكل بترول شوي بس، والشكل مهم بعد
ṣghīra? yā shēkh! il-kbīra tākil batrōl shwayy bas, w ish-shakil muhimm baʿad
Small? Come on! A big one only uses a bit more petrol, and looks matter too.
B
الشكل مب كل شي. أهم شي ما تخرب كل أسبوع
ish-shakil mub kill shay. ahamm shay ma tikhrab kill usbūʿ
Looks aren't everything. The main thing is it doesn't break down every week.
A
زين، أقنعتني. في واحد أعرفه يبيع سيارته، صغيرة ونظيفة
zēn, agnaʿtni. fī wāḥid aʿarfah ybīʿ sayyārtah, ṣghīra w naẓīfa
OK, you've convinced me. There's a guy I know selling his car; it's small and in good condition.
B
صج؟ ليش يبيعها؟ لا يكون فيها شي
ṣij? lēsh ybīʿha? la ykūn fīha shay
Really? Why's he selling it? There isn't something wrong with it, is there?
A
لا، بيسافر ويبي يبيعها بسرعة
la, biysāfir w yabi ybīʿha b-surʿa
No, he's going abroad and wants to sell it quickly.
B
زين، بس بشوفها أول، وبسوي لها فحص
zēn, bas bashūfha awwal, w basawwī-lha faḥiṣ
OK, but I'll see it first and get it inspected.
items: I don't want to spend a lot
UAE also: ma abā aṣrif (ما أبا أصرف)
nothing will stop you, nothing can stop you (to a man)
(recognise); to a woman: wala shay ywaggfich (ولا شي يوقفج)
(it, f.) uses a lot of petrol (lit. eats petrol)
clean; in good condition (a car, a flat)
I'm selling my car: abīʿ sayyārti (أبيع سيارتي)
a masculine thing: fīh shay (فيه شي)
an inspection, a check-up (of a car)
I'll get it (f.) inspected: basawwī-lha faḥiṣ (بسوي لها فحص)

title: Cash today? Now you're talking
goal: At the seller's house, look over the small car Sēf found for you, resist his pressure, and agree a small discount for paying cash after the inspection
tip: Answer pressure calmly: if he says someone else wants it, let him (khallah yākhidh-ha). Show you're serious (ana jādd), then offer what he wants most in return for what you want: idha l-faḥiṣ ṭilaʿ zēn, adfaʿ-lak kāsh il-yōm, bas tnazzil shwayy.
grammar: negotiating: calling a bluff, then trading (khallah yākhidh-ha, idha…, bas…)
dialogue: A
هذي هي. ما مشت وايد، ونظيفة من داخل ومن برا
hādhi hiya. ma mishat wāyid, w naẓīfa min dākhil w min barra
Here it is. It hasn't done many kilometres, and it's clean inside and out.
B
ما شاء الله، حلوة. بس الكفرات قديمة
mā shāʼ allāh, ḥilwa. bas il-kafarāt gadīma
Mā shāʼ allāh, it's nice. But the tyres are old.
A
الكفرات بسيطة. وترا في واحد ثاني يبيها اليوم
il-kafarāt basīṭa. w tara fī wāḥid thāni yabīha l-yōm
The tyres are nothing. And there's someone else who wants it today, you know.
B
خله ياخذها. أنا جاد، بس ما بدفع أكثر من سعرها
khallah yākhidhha. ana jādd, bas ma badfaʿ akthar min siʿrha
Let him have it. I'm serious, but I won't pay more than it's worth.
A
زين، شو تبي؟
zēn, shu tabi?
All right, what do you want?
B
إذا الفحص طلع زين، أدفع لك كاش اليوم. بس تنزل شوي عشان الكفرات
idha l-faḥiṣ ṭilaʿ zēn, adfaʿ-lak kāsh il-yōm. bas tnazzil shwayy ʿashān il-kafarāt
If the inspection comes back fine, I'll pay you cash today. But you knock a bit off for the tyres.
A
كاش اليوم؟ هذا كلام ثاني
kāsh il-yōm? hādha kalām thāni
Cash today? Now that's a different story.
B
يعني اتفقنا؟
yaʿni ittafagna?
So, is it a deal?
A
اتفقنا. ومبروك عليك من الحين!
ittafagna. w mabrūk ʿalēk min il-ḥīn!
Deal. And congratulations in advance!
B
الله يبارك فيك. الفحص باكر الصبح إن شاء الله
allāh ybārik fīk. il-faḥiṣ bāchir iṣ-ṣubḥ in shāʼ allāh
Thank you. The inspection's tomorrow morning, God willing.
items: it (f.) hasn't done many kilometres (a car; lit. it hasn't walked much)
let him have it (f.), let him take it
a masculine thing: khallah yākhdhah (خله ياخذه)
(it) came back fine, turned out fine
a feminine thing: ṭilʿat zēna (طلعت زينة)
you knock a bit off, you come down a bit (on price) (to a man)
to a woman: tnazzlīn shwayy (تنزلين شوي)
now that's a different story, now you're talking
culture: When someone shows you something new, Gulf speakers admire it with mā shāʼ allāh, to praise it without envy, and say mabrūk for the new thing; the reply is allāh ybārik fīk. So B starts with mā shāʼ allāh even while he points out the old tyres, and the seller's mabrūk closes the deal.
